$comment: The judgement calls — everything that cannot be extracted from code. Props, tokens, tests and adoption are generated; this file holds what a human decided. Keep it honest: it is what the inventory site and AGENTS.md publish.
summary: Triggers an action. The default interactive element of the system.
description: Button covers every action a user takes in place — submitting, confirming, opening an overlay, running a command. It handles focus rings, disabled and loading semantics, icon slots and hit-target sizing so callers do not have to.
useFor: Actions the user takes: save, delete, confirm, open a dialog
Icon-only affordances in dense toolbars (with a required aria-label)
dontUseFor: Navigation — use Link, or `render={<a href/>}` so it is a real anchor
Toggling a persistent binary state — use Switch or ToggleButton, which announce their state
A whole clickable card — put the button inside it, so the accessible name is the action and not the card's entire text

keyboard.action: Moves focus in; a `disabled` button is skipped, an `aria-disabled` one is not

provides: Native <button> semantics, so Enter/Space and form submission work without JS
A visible :focus-visible ring at ≥3:1 against both the button and the page
aria-busy and a screen-reader-only status while loading
aria-disabled rather than disabled while loading, so the control stays reachable and can explain itself
A ≥44px tap target via a pseudo-element, without changing the visual size
consumerMustProvide: aria-label when there is no text child — enforced by the prop types, not by review
An accessible name that describes the ACTION ('Delete project'), not the icon ('trash')
type="submit" inside a form; the default is deliberately type="button" to avoid accidental submits
limitations: A `disabled` button is invisible to screen readers browsing by control. When the reason matters, prefer keeping it enabled and explaining the failure on activation.

doDont.why: Screen-reader users often navigate by pulling up a list of buttons, out of context. Nine buttons called 'OK' is nine identical entries.
Emphasis is relative. When everything is primary, the variant carries no information and the user has to read all three.

doDont.do: Use `loading` while an action is in flight
doDont.dont: Swap the label for 'Saving…' by hand
doDont.why: `loading` keeps the width stable, announces via aria-busy, and blocks double-submits. A manual swap does none of that and reflows the row.

doDont.do: `render={<a href="/pricing" />}` for navigation styled as a button
doDont.why: An onClick handler is not a link: no middle-click, no cmd-click, no right-click 'open in new tab', no href for the status bar, and screen readers announce the wrong role.

examples.title: Variants
examples.description: Emphasis, from most to least. `danger` is for destructive actions only — overuse blunts it.
examples.code:
<Button variant="primary">Save changes</Button>
<Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button>
<Button variant="ghost">Learn more</Button>
<Button variant="danger">Delete project</Button>

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: `md` is the default and the right answer almost always. `sm` for dense toolbars, `lg` for a single prominent call to action.

examples.title: Loading
examples.description: The label stays laid out under the spinner, so the button does not resize and the row does not reflow.

examples.title: Icon only
examples.description: aria-label is required by the type — this will not compile without it.

examples.title: As a link
examples.description: Keeps the button's appearance and the anchor's behaviour.
